newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Italy could face fines over horse welfare.
newsitem.headline: Italy could face fines over horse welfare.

text.p: Italy could face fines for failing to protect horses imported from eastern Europe, the European Commission said in a statement on Tuesday.
The complaint made to the Commission is identical to one made in early 1995 which was found to be largely substantiated, the statement said.
Referring to imports of horses via three Italian border posts, Goriza, Fernetti and Prosecco, the statement said:

"The substance of the complaint is that overloaded trucks with sick, injured and dead horses arrived at these border posts and that veterinary treatment, feed, water and rest was either not provided or was totally inadequate," the statement said.
The allegations made by the Eurogroup for Animal Welfare that the Directive on the welfare of animals in transport is not being respected is to be investigated by Commission veterinary experts.
In 1995 a Commission inspection team found that similar complaints were true and the Italian authorities undertook to enforce the Directive, the statement said.

Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said in the statement that if the new complaint proves that little has changed in the past 18 months then the Commissioner will, if necessary, open infringement proceedings.
